title: Choose the visual world
question: space gets rebuilt from the ground up, so the visual world comes first. The roll's direction leads, my own top-ranked candidate sits beside it, two strong alternates follow, then four references I judged and declined, and the category standard as a quiet exit. Which world do I build?

options.label: Contact Sheet
options.lineage: darkroom contact prints of a full roll
options.thesis: See the whole roll at once, mark a frame with grease pencil, take it to the enlarger — which is exactly scan, select, zoom.
options.viewport: The scanned level contact-printed edge to edge, film rebate with live frame codes down the margin, one frame circled in chinagraph red.
options.risk: Miss the discipline and the amber rebate reads as decoration instead of live level metadata.

raised.raise: Nothing is labeled twice — the tile carries the name, the legend decodes the color once, hover supplies the rest.
One motion curve for the entire app: every transition runs 0.4s with an overshoot before it settles, declared once as a token.
Reordering is live state — sorting the rail animates rows into their new rank instead of teleporting them.
Numeric density is the ornament — packed tabular figures in the margins do the decorating, so nothing else has to.

options.label: Topographic Survey Sheet
options.thesis: The drive as surveyed territory: parcels sized by area, hypsometric tints by category, marginalia carrying every readout.
options.viewport: One sheet filling the frame — tinted parcels, hairline rules, and a marginalia block of scale bar, legend and sheet number.
options.risk: The familiar, orderly destination: legible instantly, but also where most data utilities land.

options.label: Gate Board
options.lineage: boarding passes and live departure boards
options.thesis: The scan reads as a pass strip; the rail becomes a live board whose rows rerank in place and never teleport.
options.viewport: A segmented pass strip across the top over a dense ranked board, one row lit because its value changed.
options.case: Fuses cleanly and holds identification — the largest-files rail becomes a live reranking board. Loses on clarity: a ranked board cannot organize a spatial map.
options.risk: Slides into transit cosplay the moment perforations start decorating buttons.

options.label: Graphite Console
options.thesis: Graphite panels divided by hairline seams, monospaced figures everywhere, syntax-derived accents only where state is real.
options.viewport: Persistent panels tiling the window, tabular figures in every readout, one accent reserved for the primary action.
options.case: Holds identification hard for a technical user; loses clarity because its persistent panel grid collides with the brief's ban on boxing every element into a uniform card grid.
options.risk: The category default — indistinguishable from every other system utility.

options.label: Catalog Sleeve
options.thesis: Matte black field, one white hairline plot, a coded strip of hue blocks that decodes to the name.
options.viewport: A black field with a single white line-plot owning it and a coded color strip along the foot.
options.risk: Reads as design-culture reference rather than a working tool.
options.case: Loses both axes: label-by-default refusal fights a product whose worst bug was unreadable names.
options.kept: Kept: nothing is labeled twice — hover decodes what the color already said.

options.label: Gardens Guide
options.lineage: folded zoo and gardens guide maps
options.thesis: Swelling flat lobes on cream, one coastline doing all the dividing, capsules pinned to the edge.
options.viewport: Organic lobes of flat colour with the ground showing through as water, one oversized headland crossing the fold.
options.risk: Charming at a glance, unreadable the moment area must be trusted.
options.case: Loses both axes: organic lobes destroy area accuracy and leave labels no rectangle to sit in.
options.kept: Kept: one motion curve for the whole app — 0.4s, overshoot, settle.

options.label: Goods Roster
options.thesis: A pastel roster grid where every entry carries a name plate and a ruled note beneath its portrait.
options.viewport: A ranked grid of rounded cells, each with a name plate, a figure and a one-line record ruled below.
options.risk: Bounce-on-focus turns a disk tool into a toy.
options.case: Loses both axes: it is the pastel tile grid this brief bans outright, and a ranked roster is not a map of territory.
options.kept: Kept: ranked ordering is live state — rows animate into their new rank.

options.label: Data Field
options.thesis: Pure black and white barcode columns with monospace numerals packed to the edge of the frame.
options.viewport: Dense vertical bar fields strobing to their negative, numbers packed in the margin.
options.risk: Exhibition piece; hostile as a working surface.
options.case: Loses both axes: binary-only ink kills the eight-category encoding the product depends on, and strobe motion belongs in a gallery.
options.kept: Kept: numeric density is the ornament — packed tabular figures do the decorating.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What every disk analyzer ships, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: A light dashboard of rounded cards with a pastel treemap and a stat row on top.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
